newsitem.title: IRAQ: Food supplies arrive in Iraq, U.N. says.
newsitem.headline: Food supplies arrive in Iraq, U.N. says.

text.p: Some 500 tonnes of foodstuffs bought under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the U.N. have arrived and 13,000 tonnes will reach the sanctions-hit country on Tuesday, U.N. sources said on Sunday.
A fleet of trucks carrying white beans, chickpeas and vegetable oil arrived on Saturday in northern Iraq from Turkey, a U.N. source told Reuters.
The first food shipments under the programme arrived on Wednesday.

The food arrived three months after implementation of the deal which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy humanitarian needs for Iraqis, suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The U.N. source said 13,000 tons of rice from Thailand was expected to arrive at the port of Umm Qasr on Tuesday.
Baghdad has been complaining to the U.N. that food supplies were taking too long and urged the world body to speed them up.
